Anne Hathaway.extract: American actress (born 1982) For other uses, see Anne Hathaway (disambiguation) . Anne Jacqueline Hathaway (born November 12, 1982) is an American actress. Her work encompasses both screen and stage, and her accolades include an Academy Award , a British Academy Film Award , a Golden Globe Award , a Screen Actors Guild Award , and a Primetime Emmy Award , in addition to two other Golden Globe nominations. [ a ] Her films have grossed more than $6.7 billion worldwide. As a teenager, Hathaway was cast in the television series Get Real (1999–2000). Her breakthrough came when she starred as Mia Thermopolis in her debut film, the Disney comedy The Princess Diaries (2001). In 2005, she played more mature roles in the dramas Havoc and Brokeback Mountain . The comedy The Devil Wears Prada (2006), in which Hathaway played an assistant to a fashion magazine editor, was her biggest commercial success to that point. She played a recovering alcoholic in the drama Rachel Getting Married (2008), which earned her a nomination for the Academy Award for Best Actress . She subsequently appeared in the commercially successful romantic films Bride Wars (2009), Valentine's Day (2010) and Love & Other Drugs (2010). In 2012, Hathaway starred as Selina Kyle / Catwoman in The Dark Knight Rises , her first of three collaborations with director Christopher Nolan . That year, she also played Fantine , a prostitute dying of tuberculosis , in the musical romantic drama Les Misérables , for which she earned multiple accolades, including an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress . She went on to play a scientist in Interstellar (2014), the owner of an online fashion site in The Intern (2015), a haughty actress in Ocean's 8 (2018), a single mother in The Idea of You (2024), a journalist in The Devil Wears Prada 2 (2026) and Penelope in The Odyssey (2026). In television, Hathaway won a Primetime Emmy Award for her guest voice role on The Simpsons in 2010, and starred in the miniseries WeCrashed (2022). She has sung for soundtracks and performed on the New York stage, and she advocates for gender equality as a UN Women Goodwill Ambassador . Hathaway is married to Adam Shulman, with whom she has two children. Early life and education [ edit | edit source ] Anne Jacqueline Hathaway was born on November 12, 1982, in the Brooklyn borough of New York City. [ 4 ] She is of Irish, English, German and French descent. Her father, Gerald, was a labor attorney, and her mother, Kate (née McCauley), is a former actress. [ 5 ] [ 6 ] Hathaway's maternal grandfather was the WIP (AM) Philadelphia radio personality Joe McCauley. [ 7 ] According to The Daily Telegraph , Hathaway was named after William Shakespeare's wife . [ 8 ] She has an older brother, Michael, and a younger brother, Thomas. [ 9 ] When Hathaway was six years old, the family moved to Millburn, New Jersey , where she was raised. [ 10 ] Hathaway became fascinated with the stage at age eight, [ 6 ] when she watched her mother portray the prostitute Fantine in the first national tour of Les Misérables . Hathaway's parents were not keen on allowing her to pursue an acting career, and her mother eventually quit acting to raise Hathaway and her brothers. [ 11 ] Hathaway was raised as Roman Catholic with what she considers to be "really strong values" and wished to be a nun during her childhood, but acting was always a high priority for her. [ 10 ] [ 12 ] Her relationship with the Catholic Church changed at age 15 after she learned her older brother was gay. [ 12 ] Her family left the church, joining the Episcopal Church because of its acceptance of homosexuality, but they eventually left that church too. [ 13 ] In 2009, Hathaway described her religious beliefs as "a work in progress". [ 12 ] During her youth, Hathaway appeared in several productions at Paper Mill Playhouse in Millburn, New Jersey. Hathaway attended Brooklyn Heights Montessori School and Wyoming Elementary School in Millburn. [ 14 ] She studied at the American Academy of Dramatic Arts in 1993 and became the first teenager admitted into the Barrow Group Theater Company's acting program. [ 15 ] [ 16 ] She attended Millburn High School , where she played soccer and took part in many plays, including Once Upon a Mattress , in which she portrayed Winnifred. [ 17 ] She also appeared in the plays Jane Eyre and Gigi at New Jersey's Paper Mill Playhouse . [ 18 ] Between 1998 and 1999, Hathaway sang soprano with the All-Eastern U.S. High School Honors Chorus at Carnegie Hall and acted in plays at Seton Hall Preparatory School in West Orange , New Jersey. [ 14 ] Three days after a chorus performance at Carnegie Hall, Hathaway was cast as Meghan Green in the short-lived Fox television series Get Real , alongside Jon Tenney , Debrah Farentino and Jesse Eisenberg . [ 18 ] [ 19 ] Hathaway suffered from depression and anxiety as a teenager; in 2008, she stated she had "grown from" it. [ 8 ] Hathaway spent several semesters as an English major and political science minor at Vassar College in Poughkeepsie, New York ; she missed her first semester due to the production schedule of her first film, The Princess Diaries (2001). [ 20 ] [ 18 ] She later transferred to New York University 's Gallatin School of Individualized Study . [ 20 ] Hathaway said she never regretted not completing her degree, as she enjoyed being with others who "were trying to grow up". [ 20 ] Early in Hathaway's film career, her acting style and appearance were likened to Judy Garland —whom she cites as one of her favorite actresses—and Audrey Hepburn . [ b ] Career [ edit | edit source ] 2001–2004: Early roles and breakthrough [ edit | edit source ] In 2001, Hathaway starred in the Disney comedy The Princess Diaries , based on Meg Cabot 's novel The Princess Diaries . She portrayed the teenager Mia Thermopolis , who discovers that she is the heiress to the throne of the fictional Kingdom of Genovia. Hathaway auditioned for the role during a flight layover on the way to New Zealand. [ 14 ] Director Garry Marshall initially considered Liv Tyler for the role, but cast Hathaway after his granddaughters suggested that she had the best "princess" hair. [ 24 ] The film received mixed reviews from critics but became a major commercial success, [ citation needed ] grossing $165 million worldwide. [ 25 ] [ 26 ] Ben Falk of the BBC praised Hathaway's chemistry with her co-star Julie Andrews , while Elvis Mitchell of The New York Times lauded her comic talent and called her "royalty in the making". [ 27 ] [ 28 ] For her performance, Hathaway was nominated for the MTV Movie Award for Best Breakthrough Female Performance . [ 29 ] The same year, she starred with Christopher Gorham in Mitch Davis 's adventure drama The Other Side of Heaven , which was also distributed by Disney. Inspired by John H. Groberg 's memoir In the Eye of the Storm , the film met with mostly negative reviews and was a box-office failure. [ 30 ] [ 31 ] In terms of the princess role, there is only so long that you can play those as a young lady before you start feeling really ridiculous. They are so much fun to do, I figure I might as well get the most out of them while I can. Then [I'll] go off and play all the drug addicts and the prostitutes, and all the good ones you win Oscars for a little bit later on. — Hathaway, 2004 [ 21 ] Due to the success of The Princess Diaries , People magazine named Hathaway one of its breakthrough stars of 2001. [ 32 ] In 2002, Hathaway starred in the City Center Encores! concert production of Carnival! in her New York City stage debut. She played Lili, an optimistic orphan who falls in love with a magician. She memorized almost all her lines and songs at the first read-through. [ 18 ] Critics generally praised her for holding her own against well-known actors and heralded her as a new star. [ 18 ] In a review of the musical, Charles Isherwood of Variety praised Hathaway's convincing performance, calling her the highlight of the show and "remarkably unaffected and winning". [ 33 ] Hathaway won a Clarence Derwent Award for Most Promising Female. [ 34 ] Later, she voiced the audiobook release of the first three books in The Princess Diaries novel series. [ 35 ] Over the next three years, Hathaway portrayed princesses and appeared in family-oriented films, subsequently becoming known in mainstream media as a children's role model. [ 32 ] After voicing Haru Yoshioka for the English version of The Cat Returns (2002), [ 36 ] she starred in Douglas McGrath 's comedy-drama Nicholas Nickleby (2002), which opened to generally positive reviews. [ 37 ] However, the film did not enter wide release and failed at the North American box office, grossing less than $4 million in ticket sales. [ 38 ] Hathaway next starred as Ella in the fantasy romantic comedy Ella Enchanted (2004), which was based on the novel Ella Enchanted . Hathaway had read the book when she was 16, and said the initial version of the script was much closer to the source material but did not work as a film. [ 21 ] Ella Enchanted opened to mixed reviews and performed poorly at the box office, although many critics found Hathaway "charming" in her role, according to the review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes . [ c ] Hathaway sang three songs on the film's soundtrack , including a duet with singer Jesse McCartney . [ 42 ] In 2003, Hathaway turned down the role of Christine Daaé in Joel Schumacher 's The Phantom of the Opera (2004), because the production schedule of the film overlapped with that of The Princess Diaries 2: Royal Engagement (2004). [ 34 ] When Hathaway expressed hesitation about starring in the Princess Diaries sequel, director Gary Marshall encouraged her by saying that the film would bring happiness to young girls around the world. [ 21 ] The film earned mostly negative reviews but grossed $134.7 million against a $45 million budget. [ 43 ] [ 44 ] 2005–2008: Rise to prominence [ edit | edit source ] Hathaway began taking on more mature roles to avoid typecasting . [ 32 ] She also said she needed a reprieve from being a role model for children. [ 45 ] [ new archival link needed ] After replacing Tara Strong for the voice role of Red Puckett in Hoodwinked! , [ 46 ] she starred in the drama Havoc (2005) as a spoiled socialite, appearing partially nude in some scenes. Hathaway denied that taking the role was an overt attempt to be seen as a more mature actress. [ 47 ] The film was not released in theaters in the United States due to unfavorable critical reception. [ citation needed ] In the 2005 drama Brokeback Mountain , which depicts the emotional and sexual relationship between two men, Ennis Del Mar ( Heath Ledger ) and Jack Twist ( Jake Gyllenhaal ), Hathaway played Lureen, the wife of Jack. She had been sent the script with the part of Ennis' wife in mind, but decided to audition for Lureen instead. [ 48 ] She lied during the audition about her knowledge of horseback riding so that director Ang Lee would cast her, but she did subsequently take lessons. [ 49 ] The film received critical acclaim [ 50 ] [ 51 ] and several Academy Award nominations. [ 52 ] Peter Travers of Rolling Stone wrote that Hathaway "excels at showing Lureen's journey from cutie-pie to hard case", while Todd McCarthy of Variety credited her for providing "an entertaining contrast in wifely disappointment". [ 53 ] [ 54 ] Hathaway stated that the content of Brokeback Mountain was more important than its award count, and that making the film made her more aware of the kind of stories she wanted to tell as an actor. [ 55 ] At this point, she realized she wanted to play roles that would move audiences or entertain them so thoroughly that they would forget about their own lives. [ 8 ] Hathaway at the 2007 Deauville American Film Festival Hathaway starred in The Devil Wears Prada (2006), based on Lauren Weisberger 's 2003 novel . Her character is a recent college graduate who becomes an assistant to a powerful fashion magazine editor ( Meryl Streep ). [ 10 ] Hathaway said she was "the ninth choice" for the role, which she prepared for by volunteering as an assistant at an auction house . [ 56 ] [ 57 ] She also followed a weight-loss regimen which led to crying breakdowns. [ 58 ] She stated that working on the film made her respect the fashion industry a great deal more than she did previously. [ 16 ] The Devil Wears Prada received generally positive reviews; Roger Ebert said Hathaway "makes a convincing career girl" while the critical consensus on Rotten Tomatoes found "Streep in top form and Anne Hathaway more than holding her own". [ 59 ] [ 60 ] The film became Hathaway's most popular film at the time, with a worldwide gross of over $326.5 million. [ 61 ] Hathaway was cast as the female lead in the comedy Knocked Up (2007), but dropped out because she did not agree with director Judd Apatow's decision to use real footage of a woman giving birth, according to Apatow and the film's male star Seth Rogen . [ d ] In 2007, Hathaway portrayed the English author Jane Austen in the biographical romantic drama Becoming Jane . [ 55 ] A fan of Austen since the age of 14, Hathaway prepared for the role by learning sign language , calligraphy , dance choreography and piano, and by examining Austen's letters. She moved to England a month before filming to improve her English accent. She believed that if she did not perfect her accent, people would dismiss her performance in the first five minutes of the film. [ 65 ] [ 66 ] She was nominated for a British Independent Film Award for Best Actress for the film. [ 67 ] In 2008, Hathaway starred as Agent 99 in Peter Segal 's film adaptation of Mel Brooks ' television series Get Smart . Calling the role "a childhood dream come true", Hathaway learned martial arts and dancing techniques in preparation for her performance. [ 68 ] While filming an action sequence, she suffered a shin injury that required 15 stitches. [ 8 ] Get Smart was a box office success. [ 69 ] The same year, Hathaway starred in Jonathan Demme 's drama Rachel Getting Married (2008) as a young woman who returns home for her sister's wedding after being released from drug rehabilitation. Hathaway described her character as narcissistic, and earned critical acclaim for her performance. [ 1 ] Peter Travers of Rolling Stone described her as "raw and riveting" in the role, writing that she "acts the hell out of it, achieving a state of sorrowful grace". [ 70 ] Hathaway received Academy Award , Golden Globe Award , Critics' Choice , and SAG nominations for Best Actress, winning the Critics' Choice award. [ 1 ] [ 71 ] The same year, she starred in the mystery thriller Passengers [ 72 ] and hosted an episode of the sketch comedy television show Saturday Night Live . [ 73 ] 2009–2011: Romantic comedies and hosting events [ edit | edit source ] In 2009, Hathaway was invited to join the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences . [ 74 ] The same year, she starred in the romantic comedy Bride Wars , which she described as "hideously commercial—gloriously so". [ 75 ] The film, in which she and Kate Hudson play best friends who become rivals after their weddings are scheduled on the same day, was a critical failure but was successful [ citation needed ] at the box office, and earned Hathaway a nomination for the MTV Movie Award for Best Female Performance . [ 76 ] [ 77 ] During the summer of 2010, Hathaway played the heroine Viola in a production of Shakespeare's Twelfth Night at the Delacorte Theater in New York City. [ 78 ] For her portrayal of the role, she was nominated for the Drama Desk Award for Outstanding Actress in a Play . [ 79 ] In 2010, she won a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Voice-Over Performance for providing her voice for the episode " Once Upon a Time in Springfield " of The Simpsons . [ 80 ] Hathaway voiced characters in Family Guy in 2010 and 2011. [ 81 ] [ 82 ] Hathaway at the Nobel Peace Prize Concert in 2010, which she hosted with actor Denzel Washington In 2010, Hathaway played a receptionist who dates a clerk (played by Topher Grace ) in the romantic comedy Valentine's Day , directed by Garry Marshall. The film was a commercial success, [ citation needed ] grossing more than $215 million worldwide against a budget of $52 million. [ 83 ] The same year, Hathaway played the White Queen in Tim Burton 's Alice in Wonderland alongside Helena Bonham Carter and Johnny Depp . [ 84 ] She drew inspiration from Debbie Harry and the artwork of Dan Flavin for her version of the character, which she described as "a punk-rock vegan pacifist". [ 85 ] Alice in Wonderland received mixed reviews from critics [ 86 ] but grossed $1 billion at the box office, becoming the second-highest-grossing film of 2010 . [ 87 ] Hathaway reunited with her Brokeback Mountain co-star Jake Gyllenhaal for Edward Zwick 's romantic comedy-drama Love & Other Drugs (2010), which was based on the nonfiction book Hard Sell: The Evolution of a Viagra Salesman by Jamie Reidy . Hathaway's character is a free-spirited artist with Parkinson's disease . To prepare for the film's nude scenes, Hathaway watched films featuring Kate Winslet and Penélope Cruz , both of whom she felt had performed nude scenes with sensitivity and dignity. [ 88 ] [ 89 ] Critics generally praised the film's mature depiction of romance, but were unenthusiastic about its plot. [ 90 ] Hathaway's performance, which the critic Roger Ebert called "warm" and "lovable", [ 91 ] earned her a Satellite Award and a nomination for the Golden Globe Award for Best Actress – Comedy or Musical . [ 2 ] [ 92 ] In December 2010, Hathaway and Denzel Washington attended the 2010 Nobel Peace Prize ceremony in Oslo , which honored the imprisoned Chinese writer and human rights activist Liu Xiaobo . [ 93 ] The following day, they co-hosted the Nobel Peace Prize Concert . [ 94 ] [ 95 ] Two months later, Hathaway and James Franco hosted the 83rd Academy Awards . [ 96 ] Although critics were unenthusiastic about their chemistry, [ 97 ] the pair were nominated for Outstanding Variety Special (Live) at the 63rd Primetime Emmy Awards . [ 98 ] In 2011, Hathaway voiced Jewel, a Spix's macaw from Rio de Janeiro, in the animated film Rio . The film received generally positive reviews from critics, who praised its voice acting. [ 99 ] A commercial success, [ citation needed ] it grossed more than $484 million worldwide against a budget of $90 million. [ 100 ] Later that year, Hathaway starred alongside Jim Sturgess in Lone Scherfig 's One Day , based on the 2009 novel by David Nicholls . The film tells the story of two young people who meet annually for twenty years after sharing a platonic one-night stand. Hathaway was given the script clandestinely, as One Day was set in Britain, and Scherfig was not looking for an American actress for the lead role. After an unproductive meeting with Scherfig, Hathaway left a list of songs for her. After listening to them, she cast Hathaway. [ 101 ] Hathaway later expressed regret that she may have unwittingly held a misogynistic attitude towards Scherfig and not trusted her fully because of her gender. [ 102 ] Hathaway's Yorkshire accent in the film received criticism, [ 103 ] with Suzanne Moore of BBC Radio 4 's Front Row saying that it was "all over the shop ... Sometimes she's from Scotland, sometimes she's from New York, you just can't tell". [ 104 ] One Day received mixed reviews, but became a moderate box office success. [ e ] 2012–2014: Les Miserables and Christopher Nolan films [ edit | edit source ] In 2012, Hathaway's audiobook recording of L. Frank Baum 's 1900 novel The Wonderful Wizard of Oz was released at Audible.com and garnered her an Audie Award nomination for Best Solo Narration – Female. [ 108 ] She then played the morally ambiguous cat burglar Selina Kyle / Catwoman in The Dark Knight Rises , the final film in Christopher Nolan 's The Dark Knight trilogy . [ 109 ] Hathaway thought she was auditioning for the role of Harley Quinn ; after an hour of talking with Nolan, he revealed that he was considering her for Catwoman. [ 110 ] Hathaway had to redouble her efforts at the gym to meet the requirements of the role, which she described as her most physically demanding assignment up to that point. [ 111 ] [ 112 ] She trained extensively in martial arts, and looked to Hedy Lamarr in developing her performance as Catwoman. [ 113 ] Jim Vejvoda of IGN called Hathaway "a magnetic presence" who imbues her character with "a wounded spirit and a survivor's edge that makes her feel genuine and sympathetic even when she's being naughty." [ 114 ] Hathaway won the Saturn Award for Best Supporting Actress for her performance. [ 115 ] The Dark Knight Rises was well-received by critics [ 116 ] and grossed more than $1 billion worldwide, becoming the third-highest-grossing film of 2012 . [ 117 ] Hathaway portrayed Fantine , a prostitute dying of tuberculosis , in Tom Hooper 's Les Misérables (2012), a film adaptation of the stage musical Les Misérables . [ 118 ] In preparation for the role, Hathaway consumed fewer than 500 calories a day in order to lose 25 pounds (11 kg). [ 119 ] [ 120 ] As part of her effort to inhabit Fantine's misery, Hathaway deprived herself of her husband, sending him back to the United States while she was filming in London. [ 121 ] Reviewing the film for The Washington Post , Ann Hornaday called Hathaway "the centerpiece of a movie composed entirely of centerpieces". [ 122 ] Although Hathaway herself felt lukewarm about her performance, she won the Academy Award , Golden Globe Award , Screen Actors Guild Award and BAFTA Award for Best Supporting Actress. [ 123 ] [ 3 ] In January 2013, Hathaway's rendition of "I Dreamed a Dream" reached number 69 on the Billboard Hot 100 . [ 124 ] After briefly appearing in the romantic comedy Don Jon (2013), [ 125 ] Hathaway starred in and co-produced (with her husband and others) the drama film Song One . She plays a student who begins a romantic relationship with her brother's favorite musician. Her character was originally written as a 19-year-old, but Kate Barker-Froyland, the film's writer and director, changed the character to an older woman after casting Hathaway. [ 126 ] Hathaway said she decided to produce the film because of its depiction of the healing power of music and second chances. [ 127 ] For the film's soundtrack, she provided her voice for the song "Afraid of Heights". [ 128 ] Song One premiered in the U.S. Dramatic Competition at the 30th Sundance Film Festival in January 2014. [ 129 ] It was released in theaters the following year to mixed reviews from critics, [ 130 ] and failed to recoup its $6 million budget. [ 131 ] Hathaway at a screening of Rio 2 in 2014 Hathaway reprised her role as Jewel in the animated film Rio 2 (2014), her third film with Jamie Foxx . [ 132 ] It grossed nearly five times more than its $103 million budget. [ 133 ] Hathaway's sole live-action release of 2014 was Nolan's science fiction film Interstellar , which follows a crew of astronauts who travel through a wormhole in search of a new home for mankind. She was drawn to the part of NASA scientist Amelia Brand due to the character's growth from an arrogant person to a humbler one. [ 134 ] Hathaway nearly experienced hypothermia while filming a water scene in Iceland, as the dry suit she was wearing had not been properly secured. [ 135 ] Geoffrey Macnab of The Independent described Hathaway as "affecting" in her role, [ 136 ] while James Dyer of Empire found "soulful nuance" in her performance. [ 137 ] Interstellar grossed over $701 million worldwide against a budget of $165 million, [ 138 ] and earned Hathaway a nomination for the Saturn Award for Best Actress . [ 139 ] 2015–2021: Mixed success [ edit | edit source ] Hathaway began 2015 with an appearance in the first season of the musical reality show Lip Sync Battle . In the episode, she competed against her The Devil Wears Prada co-star Emily Blunt ; she lip synced " Love " by Mary J. Blige and " Wrecking Ball " by Miley Cyrus . [ 140 ] Nancy Meyers ' The Intern was Hathaway's sole film release of 2015. It tells the story of Ben Whittaker (played by Robert De Niro ), a 70-year-old widower who becomes a senior intern at an online fashion site run by Jules Ostin (Hathaway). Hathaway had aspired to work with De Niro and Meyers, her favorite actor and director, respectively; impressed with the film's story, she auditioned for the third time for a Meyers film. [ f ] [ 142 ] The Intern received mixed reviews. [ 143 ] Glenn Kenny of RogerEbert.com called Hathaway "extremely appealing" in her role, [ 144 ] while Bilge Ebiri of New York magazine said the film "gets off on De Niro's amiability and Hathaway's sweet energy". [ 145 ] The Intern grossed $194 million worldwide against a $35 million budget. [ 146 ] Hathaway at the 2016 Toronto International Film Festival Hathaway reprised the role of the White Queen in Alice Through the Looking Glass , the 2016 sequel to Alice in Wonderland . [ 147 ] That March, it was reported that she would reprise her role for The Princess Diaries 3 ; the project was cancelled after the death of Garry Marshall , who was set to direct. [ 148 ] Hathaway is one of several actors featured on Barbra Streisand 's 2016 album Encore: Movie Partners Sing Broadway . Along with Daisy Ridley , Hathaway and Streisand performed the song " At the Ballet " from A Chorus Line ; Hathaway played the role of Maggie, one of a trio of dancers hoping to be cast in an upcoming show. [ 149 ] Her final film that year was alongside Jason Sudeikis in Nacho Vigalondo 's science fiction black comedy Colossal (2016). [ 150 ] Playing an unemployed young writer, Hathaway was the first actress to sign on at a time when the project had no financial backing. She was drawn to the genre-hopping nature of the script, later comparing it to Being John Malkovich (1999), one of her favorite films. [ 151 ] Colossal received positive reviews from critics and earned $4 million at the box office. [ 152 ] [ 153 ] After a two-year absence from the screen, Hathaway starred as a famous actress in Ocean's 8 (2018), a spin-off film of the Ocean's Eleven franchise featuring an all-female ensemble cast. [ 154 ] Co-starring Sandra Bullock and Cate Blanchett , it follows a group of criminals who plan to rob the Met Gala . Hathaway was drawn to the idea of playing someone with an immense ego and saw the role as an opportunity "to lean into all the ridiculous fame nonsense" that she tried to avoid in her everyday life. [ 155 ] She hoped the film would be profitable so that it could debunk claims that female-led films do not succeed commercially. [ 156 ] Several critics considered Hathaway a "scene stealer" among the cast. [ 157 ] Jason Di Rosso of ABC Online said the film's best moments "belong to Hathaway as the anxiety-ridden, vain and capricious starlet. She is regarded as a successful combination of comedy and pathos, portraying a celebrity affected by the pressures of fame while also demonstrating the ability to navigate and outsmart them." [ 158 ] Ocean's 8 was a box office success, [ citation needed ] grossing over $297 million worldwide against a $70 million budget. [ 159 ] Hathaway's first two films of 2019, the thriller Serenity and the comedy The Hustle , were poorly received by critics. [ 160 ] [ 161 ] In Serenity , she starred alongside her Interstellar co-star Matthew McConaughey as a woman who asks her ex-husband to kill her current abusive husband. [ 162 ] Michael O’Sullivan of The Washington Post described her performance as "cartoonish", adding that her femme fatale character was reminiscent of Jessica Rabbit from Who Framed Roger Rabbit . [ 163 ] Hathaway starred alongside Rebel Wilson in The Hustle , a remake of Dirty Rotten Scoundrels (1988). [ 164 ] The Hustle emerged as a sleeper hit . [ 165 ] Hathaway next played a woman with bipolar disorder in an episode of the Amazon Prime Video romantic anthology series Modern Love . [ 166 ] She then played the wife of Mark Ruffalo 's character in Todd Haynes ' legal drama film Dark Waters , about environmental poisoning committed by the chemical company DuPont . [ 167 ] Writing for Variety , Owen Gleiberman called her supporting performance "a piercing dance of agony and loyalty". [ 168 ] In 2019, Hathaway received a motion pictures star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame for her contributions to the film industry. [ 169 ] In 2020, Hathaway was inducted into the New Jersey Hall of Fame . [ 170 ] Her first role of the new decade was in the political thriller The Last Thing He Wanted (2020), based on the 1996 novel by Joan Didion . Hathaway considered herself to be an unlikely choice for the role of a headstrong journalist, as it differed from her own "puppy dog" personality. [ 171 ] The film received negative reviews from critics. [ 172 ] Hathaway then starred as an evil witch in The Witches , an adaptation of the 1983 children's novel by Roald Dahl . The film received mixed reviews. [ 173 ] Hathaway's performances in both films earned her nominations for Worst Actress at the 41st Golden Raspberry Awards . [ 174 ] In 2021, she starred with Chiwetel Ejiofor in the heist film Locked Down , directed by Doug Liman , which premiered on HBO Max . Set during the COVID-19 pandemic , it was shot over the course of 18 days with limited resources. [ g ] Hathaway next appeared in one episode of the Amazon Prime Video anthology series Solos . [ 178 ] 2022–present: Mainstream resurgence [ edit | edit source ] Hathaway executive produced and starred opposite Jared Leto in the Apple TV+ miniseries WeCrashed (2022), about the company WeWork . [ 179 ] [ 180 ] It received generally favorable reviews, with particular praise for Hathaway's portrayal of Rebekah Neumann . [ 181 ] Angie Han of The Hollywood Reporter commended her for resisting "the temptation to turn Rebekah into an exaggerated caricature of an entitled woo-woo type". [ 182 ] The same year, Hathaway starred in James Gray 's semi-autobiographical period drama Armageddon Time , portraying a character inspired by Gray's mother. [ 183 ] David Rooney of The Hollywood Reporter considered it to be her best performance since Rachel Getting Married , while Owen Gleiberman of Variety praised her for making her character "at once affectionate and blinkered". [ 184 ] [ 185 ] Left to right: Matt Damon , Christopher Nolan , Emma Thomas and Hathaway at the premiere of The Odyssey in New York City In her two film releases of 2023, Eileen and She Came to Me , Hathaway played emotionally troubled psychiatrists. [ 186 ] Eileen , based on Ottessa Moshfegh 's 2015 thriller novel , stars Thomasin McKenzie in the title role and premiered at the 2023 Sundance Film Festival . [ 187 ] Hathaway described the film as " Carol meets Reservoir Dogs ". [ 188 ] Ryan Lattanzio of IndieWire felt Hathaway's role was "tailor-made" for her, and thought her performance was the best of her career. [ 189 ] At the 2023 Berlin International Film Festival , Rebecca Miller 's romantic comedy She Came to Me was released. [ 190 ] Hathaway's first role of 2024 was a grieving mother coping with the loss of her son in the thriller Mothers' Instinct , [ 191 ] which is a remake of the 2018 Belgian film . [ 192 ] Because the loss of a child was her worst fear, Hathaway created a "protective layer" between herself and her character, which included asking the cast and crew to call her by her character's name. [ 193 ] Writing for The Guardian , Peter Bradshaw thought her performance was overshadowed by that of her co-star Jessica Chastain . [ 194 ] Hathaway next starred in the romantic comedy The Idea of You , based on Robinne Lee 's novel The Idea of You , playing a divorced mother who begins a romance with a younger pop star. [ 195 ] [ 196 ] Alissa Wilkinson of The New York Times thought the film "succeeds mostly because of Hathaway's performance", and praised her chemistry with co-star Nicholas Galitzine . [ 197 ] Hathaway appeared in five films in 2026. Her first was David Lowery 's Mother Mary , in which she played a pop star whose reunion with her former costume designer (played by Michaela Coel ) forces her to confront her past. [ 198 ] The film received mixed reviews. [ 199 ] [ 200 ] Hathaway next reprised the role of Andrea "Andy" Sachs in The Devil Wears Prada 2 . She and her co-stars Meryl Streep and Emily Blunt each earned a $12.5 million upfront salary for the sequel, with back-end bonuses that could push their total pay past $20 million. [ 201 ] The film received generally positive reviews, [ 202 ] with David Rooney of The Hollywood Reporter calling Hathaway "effortlessly charming in the role". [ 203 ] The Devil Wears Prada 2 and Hathaway's next release— The Odyssey , her third film with Christopher Nolan—were among the highest-grossing films of 2026 . [ 204 ] In The Odyssey , she played Penelope , the Greek queen of Ithaca , who awaits the return of her husband Odysseus ( Matt Damon ) after the Trojan War . [ 205 ] Marlow Stern of Variety described Hathaway's performance as a powerful and gritty portrayal characterized by strength and determination. [ 206 ] Hathaway's fourth film of the year was David Robert Mitchell 's science fiction film The End of Oak Street , which she starred in alongside Ewan McGregor . [ citation needed ] Hathaway's final film of 2026 is Verity , based on Colleen Hoover 's 2018 novel . Hathaway stars in the film as a best-selling author. [ 207 ] Upcoming projects [ edit | edit source ] Hathaway will star alongside Tom Cruise in Days of Thunder 2 . [ 208 ] [ 209 ] She will be reprising the role of Mia Thermopolis in a third installment of The Princess Diaries series, directed by Adele Lim . [ 210 ] Public image [ edit | edit source ] Laura Brown of Harper's Bazaar has described Hathaway as sincere, warm and funny, while John Hiscock of The Daily Telegraph has called her "well-grounded" and friendly, with a good sense of humor and an easy-going attitude. [ 211 ] [ 212 ] Nancy Meyers, who directed Hathaway in The Intern , referred to her as "wise beyond her years", while the book 365 Style described her as having a girl next door image. [ 213 ] [ 214 ] In 2008, Hathaway commented on her perceived image: "People have this idea of me as just being a very prim, professional girl, which I suppose I am, but I do cut loose and have fun in my life." [ 8 ] On another occasion, Hathaway said the public perceives her as a sweet and uninteresting "good girl" with no grit or sex appeal. [ h ] The magazines Empire , Entertainment Weekly , FHM , Los Angeles Times Magazine , Maxim , and People have included Hathaway on their lists of the most attractive celebrities, and she was featured on the cover of People magazine's annual " World's Most Beautiful " issue in 2026. [ 218 ] [ 219 ] Hathaway has promoted the fashion company Tod's and the cosmetics brand Lancôme . [ i ] After her breakthrough role in The Princess Diaries , Hathaway said she struggled to find non-princess roles that were serious. According to Jodi Guglielmi of People , Hathaway's fear of being typecast motivated her to build a versatile body of work, and her practice of extensively researching her roles has been key to her success. [ 223 ] In a 2008 article for The Daily Telegraph , Catherine Elsworth described Hathaway as "the hottest young actress in Hollywood" who was viewed as the next Julia Roberts . [ 8 ] In 2011, another Daily Telegraph writer praised Hathaway's willingness to appear in various genres of films, and in 2009 the theater critic Charles Isherwood described her as a "natural star". [ j ] Writing for Esquire in 2018, Justin Kirkland felt that many of Hathaway's strong performances had been overlooked, and described her career as "subtle brilliance that has largely gone unnoticed". [ 226 ] In 2013, after Hathaway made acceptance speeches for awards she won for Les Misérables , she received widespread criticism in the press and on social media for her demeanor, with some critics describing her as "annoying" and calling her jokes "awkward". Hathaway later explained that she feels anxious when speaking in public. She said the criticism helped her grow and become a more compassionate person. [ 227 ] [ 228 ] Forbes included Hathaway on its annual Celebrity 100 list in 2009, and ranked her as one of the world's highest-paid actresses in 2015. [ 229 ] [ 230 ] In 2017, Digital Spy named her as one of the 50 highest-grossing actors of the 21st century. [ 231 ] As of 2018 [update] , Hathaway's films have grossed $6.7 billion worldwide. [ 232 ] Advocacy [ edit | edit source ] Hathaway at the 2018 Human Rights Campaign dinner in Washington, D.C. In 2008, Hathaway won an award from the Human Rights Campaign for her philanthropy. The same year, she was honored at Elle ' s Women in Hollywood tribute and was honored for her work with Step Up Women's Network. [ k ] In 2010, she began working with the World Bank on a two-year development program called The Girl Effect , with the mission of empowering girls around the world. [ 236 ] In 2013, she narrated Girl Rising , a CNN documentary film about the power of women's education. [ 63 ] Hathaway was appointed as a UN Women Goodwill Ambassador in 2016, with the stated goal of addressing the unequal burden shouldered by women who care for children. She has also worked with the Nike Foundation to raise awareness about child marriage , [ 237 ] [ 238 ] helped vaccinate children against hepatitis A in Nicaragua , [ 239 ] and promoted the rights of women and girls in Kenya and Ethiopia . [ 240 ] Hathaway serves on the board of the Lollipop Theater Network, which brings entertainment to children in hospitals. [ 241 ] She has been involved with the charities Creative Coalition , Human Rights Campaign , and St. Jude Children's Research Hospital . [ 242 ] In 2017, she spoke on International Women's Day in favor of paid parental leave for both men and women. [ 243 ] In 2018, she collaborated with 300 women in Hollywood to launch the Time's Up initiative, which aims to protect women from harassment and discrimination. [ 244 ] Hathaway has criticized inequality in the U.S. film industry and has advocated for more professional opportunities for women in the industry. [ 245 ] In response to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine , Hathaway made donations to the Ukrainian Red Cross Society , UNICEF and Save the Children to help Ukrainians affected by the war. [ 246 ] She praised the Berlin International Film Festival in 2023 for featuring Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy , who gave a televised speech during the opening ceremony. [ 247 ] Personal life [ edit | edit source ] Relationships [ edit | edit source ] Hathaway dated the Italian real estate developer Raffaello Follieri from 2004 to 2008. [ 10 ] Follieri was investigated by the Internal Revenue Service in 2008 for failure to file required non-profit information forms. [ 248 ] He was arrested on charges of defrauding investors, including former U.S. president Bill Clinton , out of millions of dollars. [ 249 ] The FBI confiscated Hathaway's private journals from Follieri's New York City apartment as part of its investigation into his activities. [ 250 ] After pleading guilty, Follieri was sentenced to four and a half years in prison. [ 251 ] Hathaway married the actor and businessman Adam Shulman in Big Sur , California on September 29, 2012. [ 252 ] The couple sold their wedding photograph and donated the proceeds to the same-sex marriage advocacy organization Freedom to Marry . They later hosted the organization's National Engagement Party fundraiser, which raised $500,000. [ 233 ] Hathaway and Shulman own several properties, including a chalet in Southern California, which serves as their primary residence, and a penthouse on the Upper West Side of New York City. [ 253 ] Hathaway experienced a miscarriage in 2015. [ 254 ] The couple have two sons, born in 2016 and 2019. [ 255 ] [ 256 ] In June 2026, Hathaway announced that she was pregnant with their third child. [ 257 ] Political views [ edit | edit source ] Hathaway has supported various Democratic candidates during U.S. presidential elections, including Barack Obama ( 2008 , 2012 ), [ 258 ] [ 259 ] Hillary Clinton ( 2016 ), [ 260 ] Joe Biden ( 2020 ), [ 261 ] and Kamala Harris ( 2024 ). [ 262 ] She attended the 2008 Democratic National Convention , [ 258 ] and appeared at a benefit concert for the Hillary Clinton campaign in New York City in 2012. [ 263 ] Hathaway supports abortion rights , immigrant rights and gun control , [ l ] and has criticized U.S. president Donald Trump for his anti-immigration policies. [ 267 ] She is a supporter of LGBT rights , and has donated money to organizations which support the legalization of same-sex marriage . [ 268 ] [ 269 ] She has spoken out on homophobia , school bullying , transphobia and white privilege . [ 270 ] Health [ edit | edit source ] In 2007, Hathaway discussed experiencing depression during her teenage years, stating that she eventually overcame it without medication. [ 271 ] In 2008, she began smoking after a stressful summer and the end of her relationship with Follieri. [ 272 ] She eventually quit smoking, and in 2018 she quit drinking alcohol. She has been vegetarian and vegan at various points in her life. Brittany Murphy.extract: American actress and singer (1977–2009) For the song by Slayyyter, see Brittany Murphy (song) . Brittany Anne Murphy-Monjack [ 4 ] ( née Bertolotti ; November 10, 1977 – December 20, 2009) was an American actress and singer, noted for her work in comedy and drama. [ 5 ] Murphy moved to Los Angeles as a teenager and began her acting career at the age of thirteen. Her breakthrough role was Tai Frasier in Clueless (1995), followed by supporting roles in independent films such as Freeway (1996) and Bongwater (1998). She made her theatrical debut in a Broadway production of Arthur Miller 's A View from the Bridge in 1997, before starring as Daisy Randone in Girl, Interrupted (1999) and Lisa Swenson in Drop Dead Gorgeous (1999). In the 2000s she played the patient Elisabeth Burrows in Don't Say a Word (2001), alongside Michael Douglas, and Alex Latourno in 8 Mile (2002), for which she garnered critical acclaim. Her subsequent roles included Riding in Cars with Boys (2001), Spun (2002), Just Married (2003), Uptown Girls (2003), Sin City (2005), and Happy Feet (2006). She also voiced the character Luanne Platter in the animated television series King of the Hill (1997–2010). On The Ramen Girl (2008), she served as a producer in addition to acting. Her final film project was Something Wicked , released in 2014. She also dabbled in music, being able to sing and play the piano and trumpet from childhood. In the early 1990s she was part of the band Blessed Soul, alongside actor Eric Balfour . The band did not release an album. She featured on British DJ Paul Oakenfold 's single " Faster Kill Pussycat " in 2006, and in the same year covered two songs, Queen 's " Somebody to Love " and Earth, Wind & Fire 's " Boogie Wonderland ", for the soundtrack of the film Happy Feet . On December 20, 2009, Murphy died aged 32, under disputed circumstances. The coroner's verdict stated that the cause of death was pneumonia , exacerbated by anemia and addiction to several prescription medications. Five months after her death, her husband, Simon Monjack , died of the same causes. The Los Angeles County Department of Health Services had considered toxic mold emanating from their home as a possible cause of death; however, Los Angeles Deputy Coroner Ed Winter stated that there were "no indicators" that mold was a factor. In January 2012, the actress's father, Angelo Bertolotti, filed a petition in the Superior Court of California asking that the Los Angeles County Coroner's Office release hair samples from his daughter for independent testing, claiming she was poisoned; the suit was dismissed. In November 2013, he claimed that a toxicology report showed that deliberate poisoning by heavy metals, including antimony and barium , was a possible cause of death. Following her death, a series of biographical documentaries were made about her life. The Brittany Murphy Story —starring Amanda Fuller as Murphy, Sherilyn Fenn as her mother Sharon, and Eric Petersen as Monjack—aired on Lifetime on September 6, 2014. It received negative reviews from the media, who criticized Fuller's poor performance. In 2020, another documentary called Brittany Murphy: An ID Mystery aired on Investigation Discovery , in which the documentary filmmakers go into more detail about her death. A year later, the streaming service HBO Max released the two-part miniseries What Happened, Brittany Murphy? (2021), which featured several people close to the actress, including Kathy Najimy , Taryn Manning , Lisa Rieffel , and director Amy Heckerling . In 2023, the streaming service Tubi released a documentary called Gone Before Her Time: Brittany Murphy , which also explored her personal life and death. Early life [ edit | edit source ] Murphy was born Brittany Anne Bertolotti [ 6 ] on November 10, 1977, at Georgia Baptist Hospital in Atlanta, [ 7 ] [ 8 ] [ 9 ] to Sharon Kathleen Murphy [ 4 ] and Angelo Joseph Bertolotti, [ 10 ] who divorced when their daughter was three years old. [ 11 ] She was raised by her mother in Edison, New Jersey , [ 11 ] [ 8 ] [ 12 ] [ A ] and attended middle school there before moving out west. [ 13 ] Angelo during this period was arrested on charges of drug possession, later spending twelve years in prison; [ 8 ] he had dealings with the Italian mafia, operating as an entrepreneur and diplomat for organized crime families. [ 7 ] She later stated that due to Sharon's financial problems, she was food insecure and on certain occasions, she had to beg her mother to buy clothes at Kmart . [ 11 ] This would later explain Murphy's marked social investment in homeless causes, as discussed in a February 2003 article in Glamour magazine. [ 14 ] In 1991, before she started high school, the family moved to Los Angeles so that Murphy could pursue an acting career. [ 15 ] [ 16 ] [ 17 ] Murphy said her mother never tried to stifle her creativity, and she considered her mother a crucial factor in her later success: "When I asked my mom to move to California, she sold everything and moved out here for me. She always believed in me." [ 9 ] Murphy's mother is of Irish and Slovak descent, and her father is of Italian descent. [ 18 ] [ 19 ] She was raised a Baptist and later became a non-denominational Christian . [ 20 ] [ 21 ] She had two older half-brothers and a younger half-sister. [ 22 ] Acting career [ edit | edit source ] 1990s: Child acting and first roles [ edit | edit source ] In 1982, she attended the Verne Fowler School of Dance and Theater Arts in Colonia, New Jersey . [ 23 ] [ 24 ] From the age of four, she trained in singing, dancing and acting until she moved to California when she was thirteen. [ 8 ] [ 25 ] In 1987, at the age of ten, she made her theatrical debut in a production of Really Rosie [ 23 ] in which her performance was praised by her teachers; [ 8 ] and she also sang in a production of Les Misérables . [ 23 ] She stood out for being energetic when acting. She went so far as to say that "my first memories were wanting... to entertain people." [ 26 ] She debuted in 1991 playing the role of Frank's sister in one episode of the television show Murphy Brown . [ 27 ] She later got her first job in Hollywood at the age of thirteen, playing the role of Brenda Drexell in the series Drexell's Class . [ 27 ] [ 28 ] She then went on to play Molly Morgan in the TV series Almost Home . [ 29 ] She appeared as a guest star on several television series, including Parker Lewis Can't Lose , Blossom , seaQuest 2032 , Murder One and Frasier . [ 28 ] She had recurring roles on Party of Five , Boy Meets World and Sister, Sister . [ 28 ] Her breakthrough role was in her second feature film, the teen comedy Clueless (1995), directed by Amy Heckerling , which developed a cult following. [ 30 ] Filming began in November 1994, at which time she was barely seventeen years old, making her the youngest member of the cast. [ 31 ] Her performance in the film was praised by both the media and critics: [ 32 ] John Menter, an acting teacher during Murphy's childhood, said: "It wasn't until I saw her, sitting in the theater, who I felt she would be a huge star." [ 32 ] During filming, as she could not attend high school, she had educational tutors. [ 33 ] The film was a sleeper hit, grossing US$56 million against its budget of US$12 million . [ 34 ] [ 35 ] Clueless is a loose adaptation of the novel Emma (1815) by Jane Austen , and many of its characters have counterparts in the novel. [ 36 ] [ 37 ] [ 38 ] Soon after, her mother Sharon was diagnosed with breast cancer , whom she was forced to take care of after the release of Clueless . [ 39 ] [ 40 ] She made her Broadway debut in 1997 playing the role of Catherine, in a new version of Arthur Miller 's A View from the Bridge along with actors Anthony LaPaglia and Allison Janney . [ 41 ] [ 42 ] She continued with roles in Freeway (1996), with Reese Witherspoon and Kiefer Sutherland , [ 14 ] and the independent comedy Bongwater (1998). [ 43 ] In 1999, she appeared as Rivkah in the television film The Devil's Arithmetic , based on the novel of the same name by Jane Yolen and directed by Donna Deitch; filming took place in Lithuania and Canada in October 1998. [ 44 ] Her performance was praised by Variety reviewer David Kronke, stating that she "brought a strange but intriguing ethereal quality to her performance." [ 44 ] That same year she had a supporting role in James Mangold 's Girl, Interrupted , as a troubled psychiatric patient alongside Winona Ryder and Angelina Jolie . [ 14 ] She was nominated at the Young Artists Awards for Best Young Lead Actress in a Feature Film for Girl, Interrupted , on March 19, 2000. [ 45 ] She later starred as an aspiring beauty queen in Drop Dead Gorgeous . [ 14 ] She voiced the character of Luanne Platter in the Fox animated sitcom King of the Hill for the entirety of the show's original run from 1997 to 2009, and Joseph Gribble until the fifth season. [ 46 ] She later said that she enjoyed doing voice-overs because they could be done at home, jokingly saying: "You can do it even in your pajamas." [ 28 ] She was nominated for an Annie Award for voice acting for the King of the Hill episode "Movin' On Up" in 2000. [ 47 ] 2000s: Acting success, decline and final works [ edit | edit source ] Murphy at the Australian premiere of Happy Feet in December 2006 She began the 2000s playing certain roles, with Jody Marken in the thriller Cherry Falls (1999), [ 48 ] and the lead role in Don't Say a Word (2001) alongside Michael Douglas , [ 49 ] whose critical reception was negative, but his performance was praised. [ 50 ] In 2002, she played the role of Alex Latourno in the film based on the life of American rapper Eminem , 8 Mile , which received critical acclaim, [ 51 ] and was a success at the box office. [ 52 ] She appeared alongside Dakota Fanning in Uptown Girls (2003), playing Molly Gunn, a twenty-two-year-old girl whose deceased father was a musician. [ 53 ] [ B ] Filming lasted from July to September 2002, and was filmed at Silvercup Studios in New York. [ 54 ] In the same year she starred in the romantic comedy Just Married . The film did well at the box office, grossing more than 100 million dollars against a budget of 18 million, [ 55 ] but it received negative reviews from both the press and film critics, which led to them appearing as nominees in the Razzie Awards for worst actor, worst supporting actress and worst on-screen couple for both. [ 56 ] At that time her mother contracted breast cancer again, so Murphy had to take care of her again. [ 40 ] A year later she played the lead role of Stacy Holt in Little Black Book (2004); this was another critical failure, for which reviewers focused on Murphy's poor performance. [ 57 ] The film opened at number five at the North American box office, grossing US$7,075,217 in its opening weekend behind Collateral , The Village , The Bourne Supremacy and The Manchurian Candidate . [ 58 ] The film finished its run with a domestic total of US$20,698,668 and an international addition of US$1,336,164 , totaling US$22,034,832 worldwide. [ 59 ] In 2005 she appeared in Sin City , directed by Robert Rodriguez, Frank Miller and Quentin Tarantino . [ 60 ] Film critic Roger Ebert frequently praised Murphy's acting talent and comic timing, giving good reviews to several of her films and comparing her to Lucille Ball : [ 61 ] As for Brittany Murphy, for me, it goes back to the 2003 Independent Spirit Awards [where] Murphy was assigned to present one of the awards. Her task was to read the names of the five nominees, open an envelope, and reveal the name of the winner. This she turned into an opportunity for screwball improvisational comedy, by pretending she could not follow this sequence, not even after the audience shouted instructions and the stage manager came to whisper in her ear not once but twice. There were those in the audience who were dumbfounded by her stupidity. I was dumbfounded by her brilliance. [ 62 ] Murphy followed with several independent films, including Spun (2002), Neverwas (2005), and Karen Moncrieff 's The Dead Girl (2006), as well as two Edward Burns films: Sidewalks of New York (2001) and The Groomsmen (2006). She returned to voice acting with the critically acclaimed 2006 animated feature Happy Feet , as Gloria Penguin. In 2009, she was cast in the Lifetime TV movie Tribute , as the main character, Cilla. Murphy completed the thriller/drama Abandoned in June 2009 and it was released in 2010, after her death. [ 63 ] In November 2009, Murphy left the production of The Caller , which was being filmed in Puerto Rico, and was replaced by Rachelle Lefevre . Murphy denied media reports that she had been fired from the project after being difficult on set, and cited "creative differences". [ 64 ] Something Wicked , her final film, was released in 2014. [ 65 ] Music career [ edit | edit source ] Murphy performing for the crew during a USO show aboard USS Nimitz on June 19, 2003 Murphy's career also included work as a singer. She was able to learn to play an instrument in just twenty minutes of practice, and learned to play the piano and trumpet at an early age. [ 66 ] Regarding her voice, she commented: "My singing voice isn't like my speaking voice...I've just always kept it a secret and never taken credit because I wanted to learn how to work behind the microphone in a recording studio, and some of the singers don't even know it was me recording on their albums." [ 67 ] In an interview she stated that her main musical influence was the American singer Madonna : "My dreams and aspirations when I was a child for as long as I can remember was to be an entertainer. I started out in dance classes and I've always sang for as long as I can remember. When I was nine I started doing musical theater in the New Jersey area, where I'm from. The quickest way to entertain more people was to audition for commercials and that was the first thing available since it was right over the Hudson River. Madonna had a quote, 'I'm going to change the world'–that was a huge inspiration to me so I decided I was going to be my own version of Madonna when I grew up". [ 67 ] [ 68 ] Plans to release a studio album were not carried out. [ 69 ] She recorded unreleased demos that were never officially released, the song "Boomlay" was leaked on the Internet, it never completed and part of the recording was lost. [ 70 ] She was in a band called Blessed Soul with fellow actor Eric Balfour in the early 1990s. On June 6, 2006, Murphy and Paul Oakenfold released the single " Faster Kill Pussycat ", from the album A Lively Mind . The song became a club hit and hit number one on Billboard 's Hot Dance Club Play chart. [ 71 ] It also hit number seven in Oakenfold's native United Kingdom in June 2006. [ 72 ] She dabbled in music again with the release of the film Happy Feet , in which she covered Queen 's " Somebody to Love " and Earth, Wind & Fire 's " Boogie Wonderland ". Murphy said about her character, Gloria, "Oddly enough, of all the characters I've played, Gloria is the most like me. And she's a penguin! George Miller always wanted one person to do both [the speaking and the singing]. I said, 'I can sing,' and I asked him to give me a shot. I don't think he took me very seriously, because most actors say they can do most things." [ 67 ] Personal life [ edit | edit source ] Relationships and friendships [ edit | edit source ] Kutcher, Kwatinetz and Macaluso [ edit | edit source ] In late 2002, she began dating Ashton Kutcher , whom she met when they starred in Just Married . [ 73 ] The director of the production, Shawn Levy , has commented on the relationship saying: "From the minute they met, they were together, they laughed all the time, they made jokes and they looked happy". It was later revealed that they had been engaged, due to both Kutcher and Murphy wearing rings, although it was never officially confirmed. [ 74 ] She was engaged to talent manager Jeff Kwatinetz , but their relationship only lasted four months. She was subsequently with Joe Macaluso in December 2005, a production assistant she met while working on the film Little Black Book . [ 75 ] Four months after the filming of The Ramen Girl , which was in April 2006, they broke up. [ 75 ] Winona Ryder [ edit | edit source ] In the early 2000s, she was close friends with American actress Winona Ryder , who worked with her in the drama film Girl, Interrupted (1999). [ 76 ] For the Los Angeles Times in September 2001, she was more open about her friendship with Ryder, where Murphy revealed that she called Ryder her "definitive mentor". [ 77 ] Murphy said, "Before, I didn't know how actors managed to look so pretty. They have stylists, hair and makeup. I look at old photos of the premiere of Clueless and I look like a meatball on top of another meatball". [ 77 ] During a television interview, Murphy along with Ryder got into a Mercedes car and kissed mouth to mouth, [ 77 ] which led theories that Murphy was a lesbian, something she rejected. [ 78 ] For People she remarked: "This was my presentation to the media, the cover of the National Enquirer ". She also said that "we just kissed as a joke. I didn't know what to do because [the photographers] were in front of the car and it was either run them over or just stay there. Then I started making faces and suddenly I became Winona Ryder's lesbian lover". [ 77 ] After Murphy's death, Ryder revealed to Total Film that she finds it difficult to watch the film after this event: "I can't watch the movie now. Her character commits suicide in the movie, I just can't. I was very close to Brittany, even in the moments before her death". [ 76 ] Eminem [ edit | edit source ] After the release of the 2002 film 8 Mile , rumors about a possible romantic relationship between Murphy and her co-star Eminem began spreading. [ 79 ] When she was asked on the Late Show with David Letterman if they had dated, she responded: "Yes, of course" and, laughing, added: "Well, it went. It came and went". Beyond speculation, it was later confirmed that the two had no relationship. [ 79 ] In another interview with The Morning Call , she revealed that she was a big fan of Eminem: "I'm a fan of him... I think that he's very misunderstood." "He's brilliant...he's a brilliant guy," she continued. When the interviewer asked if the rapper was nervous during recordings with her, she jokingly replied, "You'd have to ask him. I don't want to appear in some song or something like that. I'm being careful." [ 80 ] On another occasion, when asked if they had "something off screen," she responded: "I'll never tell." [ C ] [ 82 ] Eminem later revealed on Vibe that Murphy's death affected him greatly and that he was terrified of dying under similar circumstances. He also said that her death "was crazy. It's crazy because for a while we were close and she was a very good person. It's crazy when you see these cases, not just hers, but all the cases that have happened in Hollywood with people in music, in acting. Famous people. Famous people dying of overdoses at alarming rates and this almost sounds like advertising." [ 83 ] Simon Monjack [ edit | edit source ] " Simon Monjack was a liar, a cheat, a thief, a sociopath , a con-artist and a narcissist , all wrapped up in one ball of dysfunction". — Mark Ebner in the 2023 documentary Gone Before Her Time: Brittany Murphy [ 84 ] Months after her relationship with Macaluso, she met Simon Monjack , a British screenwriter. [ 85 ] [ 86 ] They met during the filming of The White Hotel , where Murphy played the role of actress and Monjack as director, however, the film was not released and its production was paused. [ 87 ] [ 88 ] In the 2021 documentary What Happened, Brittany Murphy?, several of Monjack's colleagues and friends accused him of being responsible for Murphy's physical changes and also of not letting her connect with her family. [ 89 ] According to the testimony of his ex-fiancée, Elizabeth Ragsdale, Monjack "was a disturbed individual who was used to scamming people and Brittany was one of his last victims". [ 90 ] In the two-part miniseries, Ragsdale explained that Monjack told her that he suffered from spinal cancer and needed shark cartilage treatments to recover. [ 90 ] It was not until he abandoned her while Ragsdale was pregnant that she contacted Monjack's mother, Linda Monjack, and realized that the story was fake. [ 90 ] Linda, who was interviewed, defended her son in this regard, saying he had developed extreme paranoia after the death of his own father, William Monjack, from cancer: "I certainly don't think he went out and told people he had cancer. I think he believed it." [ 91 ] Before Monjack met Murphy, he was with filmmaker Allison Burnett at a public dinner, where he told the assembled guests that he was a multimillionaire, had dated Elle Macpherson and Madonna , had a collection of Ferraris and was dying of brain cancer until he purchased a treatment derived from shark fins that saved his life; however, these claims were revealed to be lies. [ 92 ] As a result of this the media suspected that she had been deceived by a cheat. [ 93 ] Actress Kathy Najimy recalled: "[People] were scared. Like, 'Who is this guy and what was happening?'", [ 94 ] "She wanted to marry him, and I said, 'Honey, it hasn't been enough'." [ 95 ] Another reporter said that Murphy's friends and family tried to persuade her to break up with Monjack at one point, but her intervention failed. [ 96 ] After that it was as if she "disappeared", according to her friend Lisa Rieffel : [ 97 ] "Simon took her away. He made sure no one could get to her." [ 97 ] The couple did not announce their engagement beforehand and rarely appeared together in public before their marriage. [ 88 ] In May 2007, they married in a private Jewish ceremony in Los Angeles. [ 98 ] [ 99 ] During the last three and a half years of her life, she, her mother, and Monjack moved in together in the same mansion that Britney Spears and Justin Timberlake had lived in, and she kept much of her old furniture. [ 100 ] Health [ edit | edit source ] "You know? Someone very important in Hollywood said that I wasn't "fuckable" enough. He said I was "huggable" but not "fuckable". So I put some extensions in my hair and that made the difference". — Murphy in 2000, talking about her physical changes for the Interview magazine. [ 101 ] [ 102 ] In the early 2000s, Murphy lost a significant amount of weight, [ 103 ] [ 104 ] which led to rumors of a cocaine addiction or that she suffered from bulimia or anorexia . [ 103 ] [ 105 ] In 2005, Murphy disputed such claims to Jane magazine, saying: "No, just for the record I have never tried it in my entire life." [ 103 ] [ 105 ] She appeared to smoke both in movies and in the making-ofs in which she appeared. A Rolling Stone journalist remarked that "she smelled of vanilla and apricots. She had a cigarette in her hand. .... After a while, she pointed out that this was only her third cigarette of the week and that, consequently, 'I don't smoke, and I'm not smoking!' But you are smoking. 'Oh, now', she said, as if only a dullard could think otherwise. ... even though she doesn't smoke and wasn't smoking, she lit her fourth cigarette of the week and began smoking it avidly, passing time in the bathroom until it was yummy time for her again." [ 106 ] She had tried to quit her addiction and was against the use of marijuana, appearing in a fifteen-minute anti-smoking campaign for young people about not smoking to more than 10,000 schools as a complement to the educational program "Right Decisions, Right Now". [ 107 ] She was also against the consumption of both marijuana and drugs. [ 108 ] At the same time, she suffered from diabetes , according to her mother. [ 109 ] Actress Melanie Lynskey , one of her friends, expressed her opinion about Murphy's physical changes. For InStyle , she stated: "I was friends with Brittany Murphy, and the way she saw herself always broke my heart: the things she felt she had to change to be a successful actress." [ 110 ] "She was perfect as she was, but people tried to present her as 'the fat one,' because when she was a very young teenager, her cheeks were a little round. People tell you that you are a particular thing, and it is very difficult to combat." [ 110 ] The problem of her weight loss was such that she became weaker, unable to stand up on her own. [ 111 ] The film director Trista Jordan recalled: "I've been around thousands of actors and I've never seen anyone that thin. Her elbows... And to get up from a chair she looked like Bambi." [ 112 ] Death [ edit | edit source ] Grave of Brittany Murphy at Forest Lawn Hollywood Hills At 8:00 a.m. on December 20, 2009, the Los Angeles Fire Department responded to "a medical request" [ 113 ] at the Los Angeles home Murphy and Monjack shared. She had apparently collapsed in a bathroom. [ 9 ] Firefighters attempted to resuscitate Murphy on the scene. She was transported to Cedars-Sinai Medical Center , where she died at 10:05 a.m. after going into cardiac arrest . [ 9 ] [ 113 ] [ 114 ] An autopsy was performed the day after she died. [ 115 ] The Los Angeles County Coroner's Office, in a report issued February 2010, said that the manner of death was accidental and that the cause of death was pneumonia, with secondary factors of severe iron-deficiency anemia and multiple drug intoxication . [ 116 ] [ 117 ] The coroner found a range of over-the-counter and prescription medications in Murphy's system, with the most likely reason being to treat a cold or respiratory infection. These included "elevated levels" of hydrocodone , which is a narcotic ; acetaminophen , L-methamphetamine , and chlorpheniramine . Hydrocodone requires a prescription while the others are over the counter. The report observed: "the possible adverse physiological effects of elevated levels of these medications cannot be discounted, especially in her weakened state." [ 116 ] On December 24, 2009, Murphy was buried at Forest Lawn Memorial Park in Hollywood Hills. [ 118 ] In January 2010, Murphy's husband, Simon Monjack , and her mother, Sharon Murphy, claimed that she did not use alcohol or other drugs, and that drugs did not cause her death; instead, they attributed it to a heart condition, mitral valve prolapse . [ 119 ] [ 120 ] [ 121 ] Death of Simon Monjack [ edit | edit source ] On May 23, 2010, Monjack was found dead at the same Hollywood Hills residence. [ 122 ] The coroner's report attributed his death to acute pneumonia and severe anemia. [ 123 ] It was reported that the Los Angeles County Department of Health had considered toxic mold in their house as a possible cause of the deaths, but this was dismissed by Los Angeles Assistant Chief Coroner Ed Winter, who stated that there were "no indicators" that mold was a factor. [ 124 ] Sharon Murphy described the reports of mold contributing to the deaths as "absurd" and went on to state that inspecting the home for mold was never requested by the Health Department. [ 125 ] In December 2011, Sharon Murphy changed her stance, announcing that toxic mold was indeed what killed her daughter and son-in-law, and filed a lawsuit against the attorneys who represented her in an earlier suit against the builders of the home where her daughter and son-in-law died. [ 126 ] In January 2012, Murphy's father, Angelo Bertolotti, applied to the Superior Court of California requesting that the Los Angeles County Coroner's Office be required to hand over samples of his daughter's hair for independent testing. [ 127 ] [ 128 ] The suit was dismissed seven months later, after Bertolotti failed to attend two separate hearings. [ 129 ] In November 2013, Bertolotti claimed that a toxicology report showed that deliberate poisoning by heavy metals, including antimony and barium , was a possible cause of his daughter's death. Sharon Murphy described the claim as "a smear". [ 130 ] [ 131 ] Brittany Murphy Foundation [ edit | edit source ] In January 2010, Murphy's mother, Sharon, and her widower, Simon Monjack, established the Brittany Murphy Foundation, a charitable fund for children's arts education, as well as supporting the USO and cancer research. [ 132 ] [ 133 ] The Foundation was launched on February 4, 2010, at a fundraising event at the Saban Theatre in Beverly Hills. [ 134 ] After a records search revealed that the foundation's not-for-profit status had not been filed, the foundation refunded the donations received. In an official letter on the foundation's website, they stated that in an effort to get the foundation set up as quickly as possible, they had established it as a private foundation with plans to apply for nonprofit status later. However, they said that they had decided to wait until the foundation's nonprofit status was approved before going any further in order to truly honor Murphy and the foundation's charitable goals. [ 135 ] On November 10, 2013, the Brittany Murphy Foundation was officially relaunched by her father Angelo Bertolotti, according to a press release posted at the foundation's website. [ 136 ] As of early 2026, the Brittany Murphy Foundation appears to be defunct. GuideStar USA, Inc. , an information service specializing in reporting on US nonprofit companies, reports that the Brittany Murphy Foundation has not appeared on the IRS Business Master File in months, which may indicate that it has ceased operations. [ 137 ] Documentaries [ edit | edit source ] Years after her death, a number of biographical documentaries were made covering her career and death. In 2020, Investigation Discovery premiered an exclusive documentary about the circumstances of Murphy's death called Brittany Murphy: An ID Mystery , which raised a number of unanswered questions, with the documentarians suggesting that her then-husband, screenwriter Simon Monjack, and her mother, Sharon Murphy, may have contributed to her death. [ 138 ] Her father appears in the documentary saying that he always believed his daughter's mother and husband were involved in both deaths, something she has denied. [ 139 ] On October 14, 2021, a two-part docuseries, What Happened, Brittany Murphy? , premiered on the streaming service HBO Max , which also covered the mystery of her death. [ 140 ] Several celebrities who knew her were present, such as Kathy Najimy , Taryn Manning , Lisa Rieffel , and Clueless director Amy Heckerling . [ 141 ] [ 142 ] Several people speculated that Monjack was actually the one constantly controlling her, preventing her from hanging out with her friends. [ 141 ] [ 93 ] Reporter Amber Ryland, who interviewed Monjack after Murphy's death, said: "I was thinking, 'Am I sitting with a killer?'" "Could he have killed his wife?" [ 143 ] Monjack's ex-fiancée, Elizabeth Ragsdale, said: "I think Simon Monjack, even if he didn't kill Brittany Murphy, allowed her to die because he didn't take her to a doctor and get her help, and I think he did the same to himself." [ 144 ] People reporter Sara Hammel commented that "if it weren't for Simon Monjack, there's a good chance Brittany Murphy would still be alive." [ 145 ] Following the premiere, Daniel Fienberg writing for The Hollywood Reporter called the documentary "20 percent a reminder of Murphy's transcendent talent, 30 percent a dead-end investigation into the mystery of her death, and 50 percent an unilluminating examination of Murphy's late husband", and concluded his review by saying that "[Murphy] deserved better than the media treatment she received, which likely contributed to [Monjack's] ability to control her the way he did." [ 146 ] The docuseries was poorly received by critics. Review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes gave it a 19% rating and stated: " What Happened, Brittany Murphy? asks big questions about a beloved star, but lacks the grace and humanity to do right by its subject's legacy." [ 147 ] Two years after the docuseries' release, Winter had died at the age of 73 of natural causes, [ 148 ] and another streaming outlet called Tubi released Gone Before Her Time: Brittany Murphy , a new biographical documentary. It features Stacey Dash (her co-star in the cult film Clueless ) among others close to Murphy. [ 149 ] Legacy [ edit | edit source ] Adam White, writing for Dazed on November 15, 2017, stated that "the actress was small, but magnetic, with the rare ability to seem completely approachable and terrifying. She had a big, bawdy laugh and acted with a manic mood mixed with breathless disbelief that things had turned out so well." [ 150 ] He went on to claim that "she was the equivalent of dancing in your room to a Spice Girls song, or crying out loud at the end of a party after too many drinks", but that "she died too young to establish an adequate legacy, and quietly for posthumous super stardom." [ 150 ] He again declared that "she was not pretty enough to be a female protagonist in an era in which lithe and ethereal Gwyneth Paltrow and Kirsten Dunst were the it girls of the moment." [ 150 ] After her death, a wide variety of friends dedicated words to her in interviews, recognizing her legacy and work within the film industry. Dakota Fanning , her co-star in the film Uptown Girls (2003), who maintained a friendship with her, said she appreciated the time they spent together both on the set of the film and at events they attended together, and that she was "very grateful to have had the opportunity to work together". [ 151 ] The song " Faster Kill Pussycat ", by British DJ Paul Oakenfold performed by Murphy, re-entered at number seven on the UK Dance Chart . [ 152 ] It also entered the UK Indie Chart in the same week, peaking at number 13. [ 153 ] In 2023, Alicia Silverstone , who was also her co-star in Clueless (1995) and was one of her friends, commented on what it was like working with Murphy during filming: I always remember when she auditioned for the part. It was the first time I was in a casting room where I was not auditioning. I was just there to help them facilitate chemistry reads. I just remember when she came in and did hers, because when she walked out of the room, I was like, "You guys! Did you see that?" As if they wouldn't know. They were like, "Yes, we saw that!" They were excited too, but it was my first time. She was just so good. — Alicia Silverstone [ 154 ] Filmography [ edit | edit source ] Films [ edit | edit source ] Television [ edit | edit source ] Video games [ edit | edit source ] Music videos [ edit | edit source ] Stage work [ edit | edit source ] Awards and nominations [ edit | edit source ] Notes [ edit | edit source ] ^ Bertolotti was not named as her father on Brittany's first death certificate.
